title: Lincoln band, Professor Jefferies and the ROTC
summary: Lincoln had a marching band and a violinist director, Professor Jefferies. Thomas hated the ROTC regimentation and uniforms.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now in Lincoln we had this group, this band here and there was a fellow, a professor out of Boston by the name of Professor Jefferies, a very fine violinist. I've been master's name was - of it pretty soon - I'll think it was 57 (sentence doesn't make sense), a very fine musician. And we got together. Now in school there are no instruments bought for you. This is your own instrument. Jeff know City, Missouri, you knew. And, they had a pretty good band there.
But, this again would be like for amateurs, would it be chiefly?

Well, this Mr. Jefferies had an idea. He liked the little concert idea and we had some violinists there and had some I think a trumpet player had come back from the first world war and a pretty well rounded band and a very fine director. So, but our band primarily was a marching band and after a few years it brought in ROTC which I distasted.(sic).
I distasted, I hated it. I hated it for a lot of reasons.
Did you have to go into that?
Well, the thing is left to you, Stan, but they were trying it. They were trying it and they gave the idea of we will try it for a couple of years.
But, now you have to make this time -- I like books. At that time I liked books. I liked to study. I liked football, I liked baseball and those sort of things. Good baseball player.
Played good tennis and all that sort of thing. And here comes regimentation some guy with some regimention. That is to say, this you've got to do.

Well, it was kind of left but the leaning was on the official side, not on our side. So, the cats would like the uniform or you know, what the hell, I mean I've got a uniform on. But, I didn't like uniforms and I'm an underclassman, I'm not an upperclassman. Some underclassmen got a chance to salute and all that. So we go out there and any guy that came through, he might be the chief street sweeper of anywhere and as long as he had an official title, we had to march. It gave this guy a chance to show off. See, I'm but still blowing my horn.
